'''Lynne Heather Walling''' (October 9, 1958 – May 28, 2021) was an American mathematician specializing in [[number theory]],<ref name=nams>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202303/noti2644/noti2644.html|title=Lynne Heather Walling (1958–2021)|first1=Jay|last1=Jorgenson|first2=Thomas|last2=Shemanske|first3=Lejla|last3=Smajlović+date=March 2023}}</ref> who became a reader in [[pure mathematics]] at the [[University of Bristol]].<ref name=home>{{cite web|url=http://www.maths.bris.ac.uk/~malhw//|location=University of Bristol|title=Lynne Walling's Home Page|accessdate=Mar 11, 2015}}</ref><ref name="University of Bristol">{{Cite web |last= Rudnev |first=Misha |date=June 15, 2021 |title=Lynne Heather Walling, 1958 - 2021 |url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/maths/news/2021/lynne-walling.html}}</ref> She was known for her research in  [[number theory]]. She died on 28 May 2021.<ref name=obit>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/inline-files/NLMS_495-for%20web.pdf|title=London Mathematical Society Newsletter}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Walling was born on October 9, 1958, and grew up in northern California. She began her undergraduate studies at the [[University of California, San Diego]], and after a two-year gap continued at [[Sonoma State University]], studying accounting at first but then finishing a bachelor's degree in mathematics.<ref name=nams/> She received her Ph.D. from [[Dartmouth College]] in 1987 under Thomas Richard Shemanske.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=38770|title=Lynne H. Walling}}</ref>

==Career and later life==
She then taught at [[St. Olaf College]], [[Minnesota]]. She lived in an old farmhouse, which had no indoor plumbing. She built a hand-operated pump, enabling her to install a bathtub in the kitchen, beside a wood-burning stove.<ref name="University of Bristol"/>

She became a [[tenure-track]] [[Assistant Professor]] at the [[University of Colorado, Boulder]] in 1990. In 1995 she received tenure, and in 2000 became a [[full Professor]]. She came to Bristol as a reader in mathematics in 2007.<ref name="University of Bristol"/> From 2011 to 2015 she was Head of Pure Mathematics, and from 2018 was Director of the Institute of Pure Mathematics.<ref name="University of Bristol"/>

==Awards and honors==

In 2012, Walling became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name=AMS>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>

==Selected publications==
* Hafner, James Lee; Walling, Lynne H. Explicit action of Hecke operators on Siegel modular forms. ''J. Number Theory'' 93 (2002), no. 1, 34–57.
* Walling, Lynne H. Hecke operators on theta series attached to lattices of arbitrary rank. ''Acta Arith.'' 54 (1990), no. 3, 213–240.
* Merrill, Kathy D.; Walling, Lynne H. Sums of squares over function fields. ''Duke Math. J.'' 71 (1993), no. 3, 665–684.
